questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was supposed to go to Australia on exchange, but it got cancelled because of Covid-19. So instead, I had the opportunity to apply for a "left-over"-spot in Europe. Because my friend was going to Charles University in Prague, I chose the same destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of information, deadlines and documents you need to keep track of. It is a bit confusing, but it is important to follow the guidelines in Mobility-One and keep an eye on emails from UCPH.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had two welcome meetings where we were given important documents and got introduced to the university - both the social and the professional aspects and opportunities. I also signed up for a "buddy" and therefor I was paired up with a local Czech student who helped me get to know the city and uni-life. That was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would recommend looking for housing as soon as possible. I used a company called "erasmusinprague". A lot of exchange-students use this company, but unfortunately it is a bit expensive compared to the housing market. Also, it was really difficult to get in touch with the company which was very frustrating. A lot of my friends using this company for housing had to move out of their apartments earlier than what the contract stated. Therefore would avoid this company.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive, but also way nicer. A lot of the dorms are a bit outside the city center, but if you find housing on your own, you can get something closer to the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was really challenging. We had one online introduction seminar on how to get registred for courses, but it was not enough and not very helpful. The online system at Charles University is pretty old and confusing. I ended up writing all the professors to ask them if they could help me get registred at their course. The professors were very helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My buddy and the professors, that I wrote on my own initiative, were helpful. Otherwise, it was pretty difficult.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was pretty succesful. But the different faculties are open for registration for courses at different times and classes startet at different times according to each faculty. Therefore, I missed the first week of some of my courses. So you should be aware of this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write to the professors whose subjects you are interested in and ask them to registrer you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 BA-level courses and 2 MA-level courses. The level of the MA-courses was ok, but the BA-courses were not that great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The facilitation of teaching was not the greates in Prague. The teaching was often characterized by randomness, lack of structure and low standards. Professors paid little attention to how they ensured that students got the most out of their lessons. In contrast, teachers in the DK are very concerned to ensure that students benefit from the lessons and that the level and quality are high.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender, Men and Masculinities

Ethnic conflicts in central and eastern Europe 

Anthropology 

The fight against totalitarian regimes om Czechoislovakia, 1939-1989 

Academic writing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The most interesting course was Gender, Men and Masculinity. The professor, Ecem, was super cool and made the teaching and course very interesting. I can definitely recommend this course!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general, I used way more money than I thought I would. You are very active and do a lot of stuff when you are on exchange, which requires money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Wine at Vinotekas are very lovely and cheap!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an organization made by local students which made a lot of activities for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to some events in the beginning - it is a good way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips outside of Prague, explore the city, go hiking and join a club or organization outside of university to meet other people!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend the "buddy"-program and joining an activity or club outside of campus - a debate club, foodball club, etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of structure.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to find housing in good time, so you get to know the housing market, the prices and the good apartments. 
Reach out to professors or coordinator by phone or email - it is way easier and they are very helpful. 
Check out the exams and demands of the courses so it fits your needs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a new city, a new culture and finding new friends all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Problems with our appartment and the communication with the owner and the company.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
